nodes.instructions:
Review line by line `src/gmst/reconcile.py`, `src/gmst/segment/endpointer.py`, `src/gmst/segment/turns.py` and `src/gmst/pipeline/stream.py` against the invariants in `CLAUDE.md` ("Streaming reconciliation") and `PLAN.md` ("`reconcile.py` edge cases", "`Segment` timestamp contract", the Ctrl-C and forced-commit rows of "Failure modes"). Read first: root `CLAUDE.md`, `PLAN.md`, `review/checkpoint-1/PLAN.md` (rules 1–8), this file. Set `status: done` before starting.

What counts as a finding: any input sequence that (a) commits a word twice, (b) makes committed spans non-monotonic, (c) re-commits a revised prefix, (d) loses text that was committed or was flushable at shutdown, (e) lets the real buffer grow past one utterance because the trim/rebase is skipped, or (f) writes to the sink from a thread other than the reconcile thread. Demonstrate each with a probe in `scripts/R1/` built on `tests/fakes.py` and the audio-reactive `_marked` / `_marked_engine` helpers in `tests/test_stream_pipeline.py` — a fixed script that ignores the audio it is handed cannot show a seam bug (CLAUDE.md "Testing"). Also check: the 600-character prompt cap, the 4000-word cap, the stall counter using the sample clock not wall time, and the second-Ctrl-C path.
nodes.findings_text:
- [blocking] After every commit the trim leaves only a sliver of the last committed word in the buffer; when the model does not re-emit that exact word first (drops the sliver, or hears a different token), `_align` returns -1 on **every** later push of the utterance, nothing is committed or even shown as a partial, the buffer grows untrimmed, and at the endpoint `flush()` drops the whole unplaceable hypothesis while `ep.reset(keep_overlap=False)` discards its audio — so the "next decode will recover it" assumption (PLAN.md "Failure modes", CLAUDE.md "Streaming reconciliation") is false: there is no next decode of that audio. With a real model this loses ~85 % of the transcript. — `src/gmst/segment/endpointer.py:88` (`n = ... int((seconds - _TRIM_BACKOFF_S) * SAMPLE_RATE)` with `seconds` = the committed word's **end**, `src/gmst/pipeline/stream.py:183`), `src/gmst/reconcile.py:49-54` (anchor must match at `hyp[0]`), `src/gmst/reconcile.py:96-97` (flush drops), `src/gmst/pipeline/stream.py:151,164,173,176` (a contradicted push leaves `last_pending == []`, so `stalled` can never fire; `keep_overlap` is false, so the audio goes too).
  - Audio-reactive fake, shipped defaults (`scripts/R1/probe_trim_fragment.py`; two 6 s marked utterances, 24 words): `[faithful] ... lost 0/24` (the `_marked_engine` assumption), `[fragment] decodes=15 committed=3 biggest_decode=7.2s ... lost 21/24`, `[dropped] ... finals: w0 w1 w20 / lost 21/24`. `biggest_decode=7.2s` vs `2.2s` also shows (e): the trim is skipped for the whole contradicted utterance.
  - Real model, shipped defaults, silero VAD, 6 LibriSpeech clips from `eval/results/data/en` (81.2 s, 197 ref words) (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 timeout 580 uv run python review/checkpoint-1/scripts/R1/probe_real_model_contradictions.py small 6`): `batch per-clip WER = 0.015`, `stream WER = 0.878 ... decodes=78 committed_words=24`, `counts: {'pushes': 78, 'contradicted': 63, 'flush_dropped_words': 174, 'flushes_dropping': 7}`; stream output `It was idle And the men of Israel And we have also There is no The crowd From rubbing shoulders with Cyril, there must`. `tiny`: batch 0.061, stream 0.873, 62/78 contradicted, first contradiction `committed tail ['idle'] | hyp head ['for', 'him', 'to', 'move', 'himself']` (the model dropped the 0.2 s sliver of "idle").
  - Attribution (tiny): not the prompt — with the prompt removed (`... tiny 6 noprompt`) stream WER 0.787, 59/78 contradicted, `committed tail ['idle'] | hyp head ['title', 'for', ...]` (sliver heard as "title"); not the back-off size — `backoff=0.6` gives stream WER 0.817, 58/78 contradicted, `committed tail ['him', 'to', 'move'] | hyp head ['himself', 'to', ...]`. The root cause is that `_align` only accepts an anchor that is an exact prefix of the new hypothesis, and every contradiction is terminal for the utterance.
  - Why the suite passes: `_marked_engine` (`tests/test_stream_pipeline.py:51-68`) decodes a 0.2 s sliver of a 0.5 s chunk as the full word, which no real model does; `tests/test_stream_realvad_slow.py:38` feeds Gaussian noise and asserts no content. The CLAUDE.md claim "verified end-to-end with real Silero VAD + tiny Whisper" (PLAN.md:283 "clean ordered transcript") does not survive real speech. Timings measured under concurrency (R2 `lid_probe.py tiny`, R5 probes running).
  - Also: the `trim_to` docstring says the cut "lands just before the word rather than inside it" (`endpointer.py:83-84`); it lands 0.2 s before the word's *end*, i.e. inside any word longer than 0.2 s.
- [serious] A second Ctrl-C that lands during an **in-loop** decode (the drain after the first Ctrl-C can hold up to `max_buffer_seconds` of queued audio) does not abandon the final decode: the `KeyboardInterrupt` unwinds the loop into `run_stream`'s `finally`, which starts the final decode anyway, now with SIGINT at `SIG_DFL`; a third Ctrl-C then kills the process without `sink.close()`, so an `--sink srt` session loses its whole file. nodes.instructions:
Walk every row of `PLAN.md` "Failure modes & degradation" and confirm the code implements its policy, citing the `file:line` that does. Files: `src/gmst/audio/{device_source,resample,file_source,types}.py`, `src/gmst/cli.py` (exit codes 0/1/2/3), `src/gmst/sink/{base,console,jsonl,srt,sse}.py`, and the shutdown path in `pipeline/stream.py`. Read first: root `CLAUDE.md`, `PLAN.md`, `review/checkpoint-1/PLAN.md` (rules 1–8), this file. Set `status: in-progress` before starting.

A row with no implementation, or an implementation that differs from the policy, is a finding. Specific checks: the capture callback does only downmix → persistent `soxr.ResampleStream` → enqueue; drop-oldest and the `[lagging]` flag reach the sink; PortAudio status flags are counted, not swallowed; `DeviceLost` after the drain → exit 3; `sink.close()` runs even when the final decode raises; the SSE per-client queue is bounded at 512 with drop-oldest and a heartbeat; the JSONL/SSE event schema matches the pinned one. You may run `gmst devices` / `gmst listen` briefly on this Linux machine; BlackHole is rule 6.
nodes.findings_text:
- [blocking] `gmst stream`'s SIGINT handling (`cli.py:169-188`) is the *only* signal trap installed.
  `grep -rn "SIGTERM" src/gmst/` returns nothing. PLAN.md's row is titled **"Ctrl-C / SIGTERM"**
  with policy "stop stream → drain queue → transcribe & flush the uncommitted tail as final → close
  sink" (`PLAN.md:164`), and CLAUDE.md repeats "without it every session loses its last utterance".
  `sigterm_probe.py` reproduces `_cmd_stream`'s exact idiom (register a SIGINT handler that runs
  cleanup; nothing for any other signal) in a child process:
  ```
  signal=SIGINT exit_code=0 stdout_after_signal='CLEANUP-RAN\n'
  signal=SIGTERM exit_code=-15 stdout_after_signal=''
  ```
  SIGTERM kills the process via Python's default disposition — no drain, no flush, no
  `sink.close()`. Any supervisor that stops the process with SIGTERM first (`systemd stop`,
  `docker stop`, plain `kill <pid>` with no `-INT`) loses the uncommitted tail — the exact loss the
  whole flush mechanism exists to prevent, on a signal the row's own title names.

- [serious] The `[lagging]` flag PLAN.md's "Bounded queues" row promises ("on full, drop oldest
  audio and set a `[lagging]` flag **the sink renders**", `PLAN.md:150`) never reaches any sink used
  by `gmst stream`. `DeviceSource.lagging`/`.stats.blocks_dropped` (`device_source.py:150-158,186-187`)
  is read in exactly one place in the whole codebase: `cli.py:118-119`, inside `_cmd_listen` — a
  different subcommand from `stream` that has no sink at all, just a level meter. `run_stream`
  (`pipeline/stream.py`) never reads `source.lagging` or `source.stats`, and `Segment`
  (`transcribe/types.py:29-37`) has no field for it, so no sink (`console.py`, `jsonl.py`, `srt.py`,
  `sse.py`) could render it even if asked. `lagging_probe.py`:
  ```
  run_stream source mentions 'lagging': False
  run_stream source mentions '.stats': False
  source.lagging = True, blocks_dropped = 7
  ...
  'lagging' appears in sink output: False
  ```
  `tests/fakes.py:70`'s `ListSource.lagging = False` is dead scaffolding — nothing in
  `test_stream_pipeline.py` ever asserts on it (`grep -n lagging tests/*.py` finds only the fakes.py
  attribute and `test_device_source.py`'s own unit test of `DeviceSource`, never a stream/CLI test).
  During a real meeting on this Linux path, a user whose queue is dropping audio gets no signal at
  all in `stream`'s console/jsonl/srt/sse output.

- [serious] PLAN.md's "PortAudio `input_overflow` / `underflow`" row says these are "counted,
  logged, never swallowed" (`PLAN.md:151`). They are counted (`device_source.py:125-128`,
  `CaptureStats.status_flags` / `.overflows`) but never logged: `grep -n "log\|Logger" src/gmst/audio/device_source.py` matches nothing, and
  `grep -rn "logging.getLogger" src/gmst/pipeline/stream.py` finds only the one call at
  `stream.py:205`, for the final-flush exception — unrelated. The counters are read in exactly the
  same one place as `lagging` above: `_cmd_listen` (`cli.py:116-117`), never in `_cmd_stream` or
  `run_stream`. A real overflow during `gmst stream` is silently invisible to the operator, contrary
  to "never swallowed".

- [serious] PLAN.md's "BlackHole / loopback not installed" row: "`gmst devices` and `gmst stream`
  print the routing setup doc and exit 2" (`PLAN.md:156`) is entirely unimplemented. `grep -rn
  "BlackHole\|routing" src/gmst/` returns nothing — the string "BlackHole" only exists in
  `README.md`. Live check on this machine:
  ```
  $ uv run gmst stream -d "definitely-not-a-real-device-xyz"
  cannot open input: no input device matching 'definitely-not-a-real-device-xyz'
  exit=1
  ```
  Every device-open failure in `_cmd_stream`/`_cmd_devices` returns exit **1** with a generic
  message (`cli.py:101-105,155-159`), matching CLAUDE.md's own exit-code table ("1: bad input — no
  such file / device") and the existing test `test_cli.py::test_stream_bad_device_returns_1` — but
  contradicting `PLAN.md`'s row, which is a distinct, never-

nodes.summary: Review `eval/build_sets.py`, `eval/run_eval.py`, `src/gmst/bench.py` and `src/gmst/metrics.py` as the instruments that will pick the default model (`CLAUDE.md` "Model default is provisional"). nodes.instructions:
Review `eval/build_sets.py`, `eval/run_eval.py`, `src/gmst/bench.py` and `src/gmst/metrics.py` as the instruments that will pick the default model (`CLAUDE.md` "Model default is provisional"). Read first: root `CLAUDE.md`, `PLAN.md`, `review/checkpoint-1/PLAN.md` (rules 1–8), this file. Set `status: done` before starting.

Questions: (1) Are the WER numbers comparable to the `egorsmkv/speech-recognition-uk` leaderboard they are meant to reproduce (same test set, same normalization — casing, punctuation, apostrophes ʼ/'/’, numerals)? (2) Do the synthetic `mixed` inter/intra clips and `real_cs` measure what they are named for, and are per-language WER and `switch_detected` computed correctly? (3) Is `gmst bench`'s "streaming amplification" the quantity `PLAN.md` "Latency budget" defines? (4) What sample size per set is needed to separate the four candidates at the leaderboard's gaps (13.7 / 20.5 / 22.8 / 12.8 % WER) — compute it, don't guess. (5) Is `eval/results/` reproducible from the scripts (the onboarding lead on `tiny` vs `large-v3`)? You may re-score from cached hypotheses (`--score-only`) and run ≤ 10 min with `tiny`; propose anything bigger as child nodes for V1.
nodes.findings_text:
- [blocking] The hypothesis cache is keyed by system name and clip id only, not by model, so `run_eval --gmst-model large-v3` silently resumes a cached `tiny` run and scores the mix as one system; no hyp record names its model — `eval/run_eval.py:273-284`, `scripts/R5/p3_cache_mixes_models.py`.
  Evidence: `done = {json.loads(x)["id"] for x in hp.read_text().splitlines() ...}` / `if m["id"] in done: continue` (run_eval.py:276, 283-284). Probe output: `records now in gmst-batch.jsonl: 18 | new decodes with large-v3: 6 | cached (tiny) records reused: 12` and `any record naming its model? False`. The only cached `gmst-batch.jsonl` today is a tiny run (its 4 en hyps score identical to `fw-tiny-*`: en WER 0.57 / CER 0.11 in all three), while the docstring says `gmst-batch FasterWhisperEngine(large-v3, ...)` (run_eval.py:6) and `--gmst-model` defaults to `large-v3` (run_eval.py:260). Answer to Q5: `scores.json` *is* reproducible from the cached hyps (`p1_rescore.py`: `rescore == scores.json: True` for all three systems), but which model produced `gmst-batch` is not recorded anywhere, and the next large-v3 run would be contaminated.
- [blocking] The default set sizes cannot separate the candidates at the leaderboard's gaps, and neither `run_eval` nor `bench` reports a confidence interval — `eval/build_sets.py:182` (`--per-lang` default 60), `src/gmst/bench.py:73-102` (one clip), `scripts/R5/p5_sample_size.py`.
  Evidence (clips needed, two-sided 95 %, 80 % power, corpus WER, cleaned-CV10 clips of 6.88 words, measured overdispersion phi = 1.90):
  `turbo-uk vs large-v2  0.97 pts: 5294 unpaired / 2893 paired (rho=0.45)`; `large-v2 vs large-v3 6.81: 132 / 73`; `large-v3 vs turbo 2.30: 1392 / 761`; `turbo-uk vs large-v3 7.78: 99 / 55`. 95 % CI half-width at WER 13.7 %: `n=4 ±17.7 pts`, `n=60 ±4.6`, `n=200 ±2.5`; bootstrap check on `small`, n=60: `[20.3, 29.6] around 24.7`. So 60 clips can at best separate {large-v2, turbo-uk} from {large-v3, turbo}; ordering within either pair needs ~800 (v3/turbo) to ~2900 (v2/turbo-uk, i.e. essentially all 3204 test clips — the leaderboard's own 1-point gap is at the edge of what that set can resolve). rho is from tiny vs small; two large-family models likely correlate more, so the paired numbers are an upper-ish bound. The n = 4 numbers in `scores.json` carry ±18-21 pts.
- [serious] `run_eval` reports the *mean of per-clip WER*, not corpus WER (total errors / total reference words), which is what the leaderboard and `jiwer.wer(list, list)` compute — so the numbers are not directly comparable to 13.72 / 20.53 / 22.83 / 12.75 — `eval/run_eval.py:210` (`_mean([_wer(m["text"], hyps[m["id"]]["text"]) for m in rows])`), `scripts/R5/p1_rescore.py`, `p5_sample_size.py`.
  Evidence: tiny-auto uk `macro=68.21 corpus=62.07`; en `macro=0.57 corpus=0.92`; on 60 clips tiny `corpus 55.69 % / macro 58.62 %`, small `24.70 % / 25.79 %`. A 1-3 pt bias is the size of the turbo-uk/large-v2 and large-v3/turbo gaps. Macro weighting also over-weights the short (4-5 word) clips.
- [serious] `real_cs` is empty and could never be non-empty: the cleaned CV10 labels contain no Latin script at all, and `run_eval` neither runs nor scores `real_cs` — `eval/build_sets.py:12-13,154-177`, `eval/run_eval.py:204,215,271`.
  Evidence: `latin rows 0` of 3204; the only non-Cyrillic characters in the labels are `{' ': 19602, "'": 163, '-': 82}`; `eval/results/data/real_cs.jsonl` is a single empty line (`real_cs manifest lines: ['']`). run_eval's sets are `{"en": "en", "uk": "uk", "mixed": None}` and `score()` iterates `("en", "uk")` and `("mixed", "mixed:inter", "mixed:intra")`. There is therefore no real code-switched audio anywhere in the harness; the docstring's "real embedded English (brand/product/person names)" does not exist in this corpus (the cleaning evidently transliterated or removed them).
